chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man takes a slave as collateral, then the slave is afflicted with loss of an eye or something from his body is diminished. Upon whom is the liability for that deficiency? He said: "Upon his master."

He said: I said: The people say that if you pledge the slave as collateral and he falls ill, or his eye bursts and he suffers a bodily deficiency, then the man's property is reduced in proportion to what is diminished from the slave. He said: "Tell me, if the slave were to kill, upon whom would his crime be?" He said: "His crime is upon his own neck."

key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the slave given as pledged property
key_terms.عَوَرٌ: loss or defect of the eye
key_terms.فِي عُنُقِهِ: resting upon him himself; attached to his own liability
key_terms.نُقْصَانُ: deficiency or diminution in value or condition
key_terms.يَرْتَهِنُ: takes as collateral in a pledge arrangement

ai.seo_question: Who bears the loss if a pledged slave is injured or physically diminished in a rahn contract?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning a slave pledged as collateral and clarifies who bears liability for bodily deficiency affecting the pledged property. Imam Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام states that the loss remains upon the slave's master, and he supports this by analogy to the slave's own criminal liability.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4096 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)) about a man who takes a slave as collateral (rahn), and the slave suffers an injury, such as losing an eye or any reduction in his physical condition. Who bears the loss for such a deficiency?
Imam (as) replied: "It is upon his master."

I said: "The people say that if you give a slave as collateral and he falls ill, loses an eye, or suffers a physical defect, the man's wealth should decrease in proportion to the loss in the slave."
Imam (as) said: "What do you think, if the slave committed murder, who would bear the liability for his crime?"
I replied: "His liability would remain upon him."
